scope_note: The 18 real-dataset terms have now each been explicitly PROPOSED and APPROVED or REJECTED by an authorized reviewer, using this codebase's own existing terminology_calibration_service lifecycle (propose_mapping/approve_mapping/reject_mapping), run once locally against a throwaway PostgreSQL database loaded from the real workbook (never committed -- see the .md report's 'Dataset boundary' note). No canonical value was invented to force an approval; a term with no genuinely exact pre-existing SIE canonical value was rejected, not approximated (see ppe_compliance_ontology_limitation below).
final_rule_compliance: Do not claim a mapping is HSE-approved unless an explicit approval operation exists and was actually exercised by an authorized reviewer. This report complies: approve_mapping() was exercised by an authorized ORG_ADMIN test-reviewer identity against the real dataset's own 3 approved terms (NearMiss, PropertyDamage, VehicleAccident), and reject_mapping() against the 15 rejected terms -- both real operations, not simulated.

ppe_compliance_ontology_limitation.why_not_semantically_exact: PPE_ISSUE (aliases 'ppe issue'/'ppe non compliance') denotes a specific negative finding/instance of non-compliance. 'PPE Compliance' is the source sheet's own Observation Category label -- a broad topic covering PPE-related observations generally, not exclusively non-compliant ones. Approving PPE_ISSUE would silently assume all 117 records were negative findings, an approximate-category substitution this milestone explicitly forbids.
ppe_compliance_ontology_limitation.action_taken: Left REJECTED/quarantined; not represented safely by the current ontology. No new canonical value invented.
ppe_compliance_ontology_limitation.recommendation: A future, deliberate ontology-review milestone could add a dedicated 'PPE compliance topic/category' Observation-subtype value distinct from PPE_ISSUE -- out of this milestone's explicit scope.

compound_event_subtype_mechanism.why_needed: The real workbook's Incident sheet (app/validation/real_dataset_loader.py) has no subtype-bearing column at all -- only event_type is populated for Incident-sheet rows. Without a compound target, an event_type-only decision for NearMiss/PropertyDamage/VehicleAccident could only ever resolve event_type, collapsing all three (plus the already-MAPPED Injury term) into an indistinguishable event_type=INCIDENT.
compound_event_subtype_mechanism.how_it_works: An event_type-domain TerminologyMappingDecision may declare provenance['target_event_subtype'], validated against the union of the existing INCIDENT subtype vocabulary and the top-level SafetyEventType names before approval (never an invented value). Applied by the adapter/reprocessing service ONLY when the record's own raw event_subtype is empty -- a genuine independent raw subtype value always takes precedence.
compound_event_subtype_mechanism.no_migration: Rides entirely on TerminologyMappingDecision.provenance, the existing JSON column already used for version-supersession bookkeeping.
canonical_values_reused_not_invented: NEAR_MISS (existing SafetyEventType, reused as a compound subtype target)

covers: versioning (open_new_version, full history preserved, including compound target_event_subtype carry-forward)
APPROVED becomes eligible; REJECTED can never be reprocessed
explicit historical reprocessing (tenant/source scoped, requires APPROVED, fresh ingestion_time)
reprocessing is idempotent (second run updates 0 records)
provenance (raw term -> exact decision_id/mapping_version -> canonical event -> feature/intelligence)
historical provenance immutable across mapping versions
compound event_type+subtype target: valid succeeds, invalid/invented fails, applied only when no independent raw subtype exists
reproducibility (same input + mapping version -> same classification)
no arbitrary canonical value can become active; no ontology value created merely to force a mapping

architecture_limitations_discovered: A plain re-ingest can never re-trigger reclassification for content that has not changed (SafetyEventIngestionService idempotency compares the raw payload hash, not its resolution) -- reprocessing must call validate_and_normalize()/_apply() directly, not re-run ingest_batch().
training_status/maintenance_status domains have no ingestion adapter that gates classification on them -- calibration approval for those domains has nothing to unlock; reprocessing refuses them.

DataSourceAdapter.validate()/normalize() take no database session by design, so the calibration-aware adapter requires a precomputed active-mapping index rebuilt once per ingestion batch, not a live query.

The real workbook's Incident sheet provides no subtype-bearing raw column at all (this milestone's finding) -- addressed via the compound event_type+subtype target mechanism, never by modifying the ingestion format.

SIE's OBSERVATION canonical subtype vocabulary has no dedicated value for the broader 'PPE compliance' topic distinct from the narrower PPE_ISSUE (this milestone's finding) -- see ppe_compliance_ontology_limitation.
recommendations_for_next_milestone: A deliberate ontology-review milestone to decide whether OBSERVATION should gain a dedicated 'PPE compliance topic' canonical value, and whether any of the other 14 rejected terms warrant a genuinely new canonical value.
A minimal API router (app/api/v1/terminology_calibration.py) so a real reviewer can drive the lifecycle from the product UI rather than a script.
The 437 records for the 15 rejected terms remain quarantined by design -- no further action expected unless a future ontology-review milestone changes the underlying vocabulary.
